name: fix_python_late_binding_closure
description: Fixes late-binding closures in a loop so each generated function uses its own index
prompts: make_multipliers(n) in builders.py should return a list of n functions where the i-th function multiplies its argument by i (so make_multipliers(4) yields functions that multiply by 0, 1, 2, 3). It's broken by Python's late-binding closures: each lambda captures the loop variable i by reference, so after the loop they ALL use the final value of i. Fix make_multipliers so each function multiplies by its own index (e.g. bind i via a default argument, or a factory function). Keep the function name and signature.

setup_files.builders.py:
def make_multipliers(n):
    """Return n functions; the i-th multiplies its argument by i."""
    # BUG: each lambda closes over the loop variable i by reference, so they
    # all end up using the final value of i.
    funcs = []
    for i in range(n):
        funcs.append(lambda x: x * i)
    return funcs
